description:
Step inside the literal birthplace of Silicon Valley! Forbes' Kerry Dolan sits down with HP Interim CEO Bruce Broussard inside the legendary 1938 HP Garage in Palo Alto to discuss the past, present, and future of American innovation. In celebration of the Forbes 250 Greatest Innovators list, Broussard shares untold stories about tech history (including a surprising connection between HP and a 12-year-old Steve Jobs), explores why true innovators aren't actually driven by money and breaks down the critical debate between government funding and private capital in the age of AI.

author: Forbes
description:
Why are so many people rethinking retirement?
In this episode of The Work Hotline, Sho Dewan (your Work Hype Man, former recruiter, and founder of Workhap) dives into a surprising trend: 61% of Americans say they don't plan to fully retire anymore.
Instead of the traditional "work until 65 and stop," more people are choosing consulting, freelancing, passion projects, part-time work, and second careers. Retirement is evolving from an ending into something much more flexible.
Sho breaks down the cultural shift happening around retirement, why more people are redefining work later in life, and what younger generations can learn from it right now. Plus, he answers real calls from listeners navigating career transitions, burnout, and the question many professionals are quietly asking themselves:
"What do I actually want my life to look like?"
Because maybe success was never meant to be one straight line, maybe you're allowed to evolve.

author: Forbes
description:
Rocket ships. AI chips. Chinese food. Clothing. Construction. Chatbots. America’s self-made women billionaires have found dozens of ways to prosper. In our first listing focusing just on those with 10-figure fortunes, Forbes found 43 self-made queens of capitalism, up from 38 a year ago as many of their businesses hit new highs. That’s despite the passing of two legendary women, Gap cofounder Doris Fisher (d. May 2026 at age 94) and Bio-Rad Laboratories' Alice Schwartz (d. September 2025, 99). Among the new billionaires are Beyonce Carter-Knowles, who climbs into the ranks on the back of her 2025 Cowboy Carter Tour; Nvidia CFO Colette Kress, who’s benefitting from the AI boom; Caryn Seidman-Becker, who runs Clear Secure, an ID technology outfit used for security checkpoints at airports, among other places; and Luana Lopes Lara, the 30-year-old Brazilian ballerina and MIT graduate who cofounded prediction market firm Kalshi.

Read the full story on Forbes: https://www.forbes.com/lists/
title: America's Richest Self-Made Women 2026
